_comment: Keys are alley numbers as strings. Scores are integers 1-10.

_example.notes: Your written notes about this alley go here.

1001.notes: My FIRST alley review, and oh lawd it's a doozy. Public Alley 1001 is one of only two alleys with a 4 digit number. This alley is sandwiched between Wentworth lecture halls and a collection of brownstone apartment buildings. Each apartment building comes complete with a 3-story wooden staircase for use in emergencies. Despite being next to Huntington Avenue it was surprisingly quiet and featured a variety of green spaces and even 2 picnic tables. I think the proximity to Wentworth contributed to its overall cleanliness; but even despite that, there were some interesting features of this alley. For one, there is a faded recreation of Edmund Tarbell's,Mother and Child in a Boat, with a matching tag and desription that I believe is pulled from the nearby MFA. Additionally, I spotted a bumper sticker on a parked car with the text 'All people are created equal members of ONE HUMAN FAMILY' following the link at the bottom led me to stumble upon the following delightful story. There was already some evidence of now faded graffiti and general art being done within the space. I got the impression that this alley primarily serves as a shortcut, a delivery location, and a parking lot; with notable secondary uses as a gathering and art space. Overall, fantastic alley. Would highly recommend checking it out and vibing there.

804.notes: Alley 804 gives street more than alley. Its nicely located off a main road, and is behind two distinct developments. There are some eclectic backyards and attempts to make the alleyway engaging and well used; however, these attempts are largely private situated behind fences or gates. In addition, I did find a clearly abandoned car that appears to have been languishing there for a long amount of time. There is a small playground there but again has a very aggressive gate indicating it is private. Vibier than some other alleys, but not S-tier. Potential for art is slightly high given the walls and vibey neighbors; but it still has a way to go.

802.notes: 802 is *chopped*. This alley should not classify as an alley, it's a glorified parking lot. One side is completely gated off and the other is just rows of parking spots. For shame. I don't think this should classify as an alley.Vibe is a 2 because it has a cool tree and a nice view of the nearby church. Smh doesn't even have a sign. I have to stop writing, I'm getting worked up.

714.notes: Interesting. Certainly one of the shortest labeled alleys I've come across yet. When I biked through it the first time, a dude was clearly peeing against the garage of the new apartment building. It does have some interesting merit for clearly segmenting 'old' and 'new' Boston. Only really useful as a conduit for Alley 716.

716.notes: Now this is an alley. Long, straight, and festooned with natural wildlife and patios galore. I saw 2 whole individuals using this patio during my trip, the first was relaxing on a bench and the second was using a grill outside. Welcoming and secluded, truly a pleasure to experience. Only downside is how it feels like its primary utilization is for parking and the neighborhood does not seem amenable to graffiti.

718.notes: Alley 718 is really the Alley 714 to Alley 719 (if you know, you know). Again, tiny alley that merely serves to link Alley 719 to the outside world. What is interesting about this, is that like 714; alley 718 has on one side an old brownstone and the other a 'new' brownstone. What differentiates the newer devlopment is they clearly made an effort to blend in with the existing infrastructure. So slightly more vibe points.

719.notes: Alley 719 is the sister alley to Alley 716. Identical layout and very similar vibes. Importantly, two things I noticed that I don't love. The first, is that most of their trees are behind fences and not part of the public location of the alley. Second, is that these buildings had a noticable dearth of patios compared to Alley 716. Both of these complaints are fixable, and I hope the good residents of Alley 719 take my suggestions to heart. I DID stubmle across one of the coolest structures/buildings here. It had a creeper vine growing over the building and hanging off a covered parking/patio area. Super cool, would LOVE to use this. It also had this beauytiful square cutout serving as a skylight.
